title: I'm making LLMs work on small and old devices
lede: smolmaxxing patches llama.cpp to run the largest model each spare device can handle, getting 8B and 16B mixture-of-experts models onto a TV box and an old iPad with about 1 GB of RAM.

points: A Xiaomi TV box and a first-generation iPad Air run 16B MoE models; an 8 GB Android phone runs 35B and 80B ones.
Frequently used experts stay in RAM while the rest are read from flash on demand, with the next layer prefetched.
Custom 1-bit, 2-bit and ternary kernels target Cortex-A55 and A7 chips, including ones without dot-product instructions.
Rarely used vocabulary rows are dropped to save memory, and every figure was measured on the device itself.
Released under MIT, with the modified models on Hugging Face.

points.text: One commenter says frontier coding agents can now port inference to old hardware from a single prompt; the author replies it took over 150 experiments to find what runs fastest.
Commenters question what models this small are good for, with one reply calling them too weak for tools or simple questions.
Others share how fast small models have improved, including a 6.5M-parameter model that reasons and calls tools.
Readers point to similar stunts, such as a TinyStories model running on a Nintendo Wii.
